chunks: And through its chain of narration, from Ali (peace be upon him), he said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) handed me the flag on the day of Khaybar, and I did not cease [fighting] until God granted victory through my hands.

key_terms.الرَّايَةَ: The flag or standard of the army
key_terms.يَوْمَ خَيْبَرَ: The day of Khaybar (a specific historical event/battle)

ai.seo_question: Who was given the flag of the Prophet at the Battle of Khaybar?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib’s pivotal role as the standard-bearer at Khaybar, a key event in Shia historiography that underscores his military prowess and divine favor. The phrase 'until God granted victory through his efforts' (fataha Allahu bi-yadi) is often interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating that the conquest was directly facilitated by Ali’s leadership, reinforcing his status as the true successor and commander. This event is frequently cited to validate the concept of Imamate, linking spiritual authority with temporal leadership.
